title: What Mike Vrabel said about his viral challenge flag toss
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: Mike Vrabel plans to retain his challenge flag duties despite the NFL rule allowing delegation to other staff.
Vrabel's challenge flag toss in the Patriots' preseason opener against the Colts gained significant social media attention.
Vrabel won his recent challenge in the game, overturning a ruling to credit the Patriots with a fumble recovery.

title: 16 hospitalized after chemical incident at Mass. industrial worksite
author: Audrey Cooney
bullets: 16 employees hospitalized after a chemical incident at an industrial worksite in Hudson on Thursday.
Hudson Fire Department suspects a chemical process caused symptoms like dizziness and eye irritation.
Firefighters from Marlborough, Stowe, Maynard, and Berlin provided mutual aid during the incident.

title: 2 New England spots make NYT’s list of best Mexican restaurants
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Tuxpan Taqueria in Central Falls, Rhode Island named one of the best Mexican restaurants by The New York Times.
Food Truck Paradise in New Haven, Connecticut also recognized, featuring 28 food trucks with diverse culinary offerings.
Tuxpan Taqueria lauded for standout tacos and unique chicken Milanesa torta on a Portuguese roll.

title: Are tire rotations necessary for electric vehicles?
author: John Paul
bullets: EVs wear tires more quickly due to instant torque and weight, making regular tire rotations crucial.
Rotating tires at recommended intervals maximizes tread life and reduces noise, even if wear seems even.
Low-rolling-resistance tires and EV characteristics often lead to shorter tire lifespans compared to gas vehicles.

title: Patriots place Terrell Jennings on IR, sign two more running backs
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: Patriots placed running back Terrell Jennings on injured reserve; his injury is undisclosed.
JaMychal Hasty and Hasan Haskins signed by Patriots to compete for third running back spot.
Running back Myles Montgomery also placed on injured reserve, impacting Patriots' backfield depth.

title: Celtics release 2026-27 schedule: When will Jaylen Brown return to Boston?
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: The Boston Celtics will start their 2026-27 NBA season on Oct. 20 with a game against the Detroit Pistons.
Jaylen Brown's return to Boston, now with the Philadelphia 76ers, is set for Jan. 21, 2027.
The Celtics' 2026-27 schedule includes 27 nationally televised games, starting with a home opener on Oct. 23 against the New York Knicks.

title: Payton Tolle pitches 8-inning gem as Red Sox end 5-game skid with 7-0 win over Blue Jays
author: The Associated Press
bullets: Payton Tolle pitched eight innings, allowing two hits, as the Red Sox defeated the Blue Jays 7-0.
Caleb Durbin hit a grand slam in the eighth inning, expanding the Red Sox lead over the Blue Jays.
Max Scherzer pitched five innings for Toronto, reaching over 3,000 career innings during the game.

title: 7 takeaways from Patriots’ 13-13 tie with Colts in preseason opener
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: The New England Patriots tied 13-13 with the Indianapolis Colts in their preseason opener, with many starters sitting out.
Veteran Patriots defenders Kindle Vildor, Jeremiah Pharms Jr., and K.J. Britt forced critical turnovers against the Colts.
Patriots kicker Andy Borregales struggled, missing three of five field-goal attempts in the preseason game.

title: Cape Cod documentarian Mischa Richter creates a dreamy ode to Grateful Dead culture with ‘Summer Tour’
author: Lauren Daley
bullets: Mischa Richter's documentary 'Summer Tour' explores Grateful Dead culture and follows two young Deadheads during Dead & Co.'s final tour.
Chloë Sevigny co-produced the film, which premiered at Telluride in 2025 and features Q&A screenings in New England in August and September.
Richter, a Provincetown resident, draws on his personal ties to the Dead community and his unique background in creating the documentary.

title: Tiffani Faison to close Sweet Cheeks Q and Fool’s Errand in the Fenway
author: Nathan Tavares
bullets: Tiffani Faison will close Sweet Cheeks Q and Fool's Errand in Fenway by November 24, after 15 years.
Closures attributed to rising operational costs, including fuel charges and ingredient tariffs, making restaurants cost-prohibitive.
Faison seeks a new location for Sweet Cheeks and plans to relocate employees within her Big Heart Hospitality group.
